An EMG performed only after the initiation of diazepam and baclofen in February 1996 was read as normal, and two subsequent EMGs performed in October 1996 and July 1997 during continued treatment were also read as normal.

Plasmapheresis over 28 months has continued to maintain lower plasma levels of GAD65 autoantibodies and controlled clinical symptoms of SMS; temporarily stopping plasmapheresis resulted in the rebound of GAD65 autoantibody levels and significantly increased stiffness and spasms. Restoring treatment caused symptom regression.

An agonist of GABA transmission such as diazepam or baclofen is the current treatment for patients with SMS [1–3]. [...] The patient continued to receive plasmapheresis (1/week), intrathecal baclofen and diazepam 5 mg/day with stabilization of stiffness and muscular pain.

Initial treatment was a combination of diazepam, baclofen, and prednisone. Due to continued pain and stiffness she began plasmapheresis and additional immunomodulatory treatment with MMF, IVIG, and cyclophosphamide. [...] plasmapheresis began in March 1996 and was performed three times per week, MMF was given at 2 g/day, and prednisone was increased to 60 mg/day in addition to diazepam and baclofen. [...] In order to further decrease GAD65 autoantibody levels as well as the frequency of plasmapheresis to improve quality of life, she received IVIG at the dose of 0.5 g/kg once per week while continuing other therapies in late June 1996. [...] During cyclophosphamide treatment she continued to take prednisone (10 mg/day) and high-dose baclofen (300 mg/day) without diazepam

extractions.value: prednisone had already been started at 10 mg/day in July 1994 to treat a severe insulin resistance. plasmapheresis began in March 1996 and was performed three times per week, MMF was given at 2 g/day, and prednisone was increased to 60 mg/day in addition to diazepam and baclofen. In order to further decrease GAD65 autoantibody levels as well as the frequency of plasmapheresis to improve quality of life, she received IVIG at the dose of 0.5 g/kg once per week while continuing other therapies in late June 1996. Due to her increased mobility, plasmapheresis was reduced to twice per week and prednisone tapered to 10 mg/day by May 1996. [...] Following a protocol similar to that for treating systemic lupus erythematosus with plasmaphereis, she received an intravenous infusion of 1700 mg cyclophosphamide after three consecutive plasmaphereses on 11 September 1996. Plasmapheresis was then stopped for 3 weeks. Due to the development of neutropenia, oral cyclophosphamide (50 mg/day) was not begun until 27 September 1996. She was then treated with oral cyclophosphamide for 2 weeks.
